key_insight: Schrödingerisation enables quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves with absorbing sponge boundaries and explicit polynomial-size damping circuits.
engineering_relevance: This approach lets quantum wave simulations model open domains while reducing artificial boundary reflections.
method: Add graded damping to every wave field in first-order acoustic and elastic equations.
Use one auxiliary variable to transform dissipative dynamics into unitary evolutions.
Factor the damping step exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates.
evidence_signal: An independent finite-difference solver found all-field damping more effective than velocity-only damping, and gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agreed with classical damped-wave solutions.
watch_item: Recovery succeeds with probability about 0.4 times the remaining energy fraction, so strong absorption can increase sampling costs.
paper_title: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schrödingerisation: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits
